what_happened: In job 6qme, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job moves code between modules. The reading had a criterion that checked callers by relying on the producer's report. The verifier never sees that report, so it could not judge the criterion. The user replaced it with two checks the verifier can run itself. One is a Grep showing that no file outside the moved module's directory names a moved item by its old module path. The other compares the test list before and after the move, using cargo test -- --list output. This is the third time in a row the same correction was needed, after vrsk and yckz.
cause: Two corrections of this exact flaw have not changed anything in the reading stage. The user's fix is applied to one job's reading and then lost. The reading stage has no rule that each criterion must name evidence the verifier can observe itself (the snapshot, commands it runs, its own tools). It is not told the producer's report is invisible to the verifier. Nothing checks a criterion's evidence source before the reading is accepted. For module-move jobs, citing the report is the default way to check callers, so it recurs. Only the user, who knows what the verifier sees, catches it.
prevention: Add two things. (1) A rule in the reader brief: every criterion must name evidence the verifier can observe itself, the producer's report is never evidence, and for code-move jobs the standard criteria are a Grep for old module paths outside the moved directory plus a before/after comparison of cargo test -- --list output. (2) A check on the reading before acceptance that rejects any criterion whose evidence refers to the producer's report, or that gives no verifier-runnable command or tool. This covers the whole class, not just module moves.
proposed_request: Make the reading stage refuse criteria that depend on evidence the verifier cannot see. Outcome: when Athena drafts a reading, every acceptance criterion names evidence the verifier can observe itself: the snapshot, commands the verifier runs, or its own tools (Read, Grep). No criterion may rest on the producer's report. Add this rule to the reader brief, and say that for jobs that move code between modules the default criteria are (a) a Grep showing no file outside the moved module's directory names a moved item by its old module path, and (b) a comparison of cargo test -- --list output before and after the move. Add a code check run on the draft reading that flags any criterion whose evidence cites the producer's report or names no verifier-runnable command, and sends the reading back for revision before it is accepted. Tests: a reading with a report-based criterion is flagged; a reading with the Grep and test-list criteria passes; the reader brief stays within its token budget; the briefs for roles switched off in athena.toml are not touched.
